name: Supplier Skid and Box Details
listdetail: This API serves as a communication channel between the Toyota Shipping Confirmation System (TSCS) and various internal systems such as Freight Verification Module (FVM), Internal Logistics Management System (ILMS), Trade Compliance, as well as external clients like the Toyota Motor Manufacturing Canada - Material Information Tracking system. It provides detailed planned shipment data at the skid/pallet and box levels, replacing the existing One Way Kanban (OWK) data. It has two main functions: Skid Details: Provides pallet-level shipment information for downstream systems to support logistics planning and tracking. Box Details: Offers box-level shipment data to enhance visibility and accuracy in shipment processing. By delivering granular shipment details, this API enables efficient coordination and synchronization across Toyota’s logistics network, ensuring timely and accurate shipment confirmations. 1. Supplier Skid and Box Details: Provides detailed planned shipment data (skid/pallet and box level) from Toyota to suppliers and internal systems and sets the foundation by communicating what needs to be shipped, where, and how. 2. Supplier Pallet Build and Load Shipment Confirmation : Suppliers use this API to confirm pallet building and shipment loading based on the planned data received. 3. Logistics Driver Validation and Route Tracking : Validates drivers authorized to perform pickups using invitation codes and provides route details and enables real-time tracking of driver pickup activities, ensuring shipments are collected as planned. 4. Driver Route and Shipment Status : Provides Toyota plants with real-time updates on driver location, order status changes, schedule alerts, and event notifications during shipment transit. This API delivers critical metrics such as mileage, transit time, and efficiency gaps, enabling plants to monitor shipment progress and respond promptly to any disruptions. 5. Abnormal Logistics Events Monitoring : Monitors for any abnormal events or disruptions during shipment transit (e.g., delays, shortages).

name: Trailer Status
listdetail: The Trailer Status API tracks trailer movement and dock activity within the warehouse yard. It delivers critical information such as trailer arrival and departure times, dock door assignments, equipment ID, Carrier Alpha Code (SCAC), shipment type, and complete route details. The service also provides metadata such as transaction ID, action codes (e.g., arrival, departure, change), and the managing organization. This API is essential for managing dock scheduling, trailer flow, and real-time visibility of trailer positioning across the facility. To track updates during the shipment prep stage, especially as trailers are being loaded, sealed, or moved for departure, please refer to the Shipment Equipment Status and Location Update API.

name: Toyota Customer Loyalty Models
listdetail: The Toyota Customer Loyalty Models predict the probability of a customer returning for a service or purchase of a new vehicle. This is relevant for all customers who currently own or have owned a Toyota in the past. Customers who repair or buy parts from a Toyota Dealer have a higher likelihood of buying another Toyota or Lexus vehicle. There are currently four models available for this feature. Model 1: Toyota Return to Service Visit Model (Binary) This is a binary classifier that predicts if a customer will return to an authorized service center for service. Model 2: Toyota Return to Service Revenue Model (5 Class Multi-class) This is a multi-class classifier that predicts the spending potential of a customer after the customer is predicted to return for a service. This generates the probabilities for 5 different classes and based on the highest probability the customer is predicted for the given class. Model 3: Toyota Return to Purchase Visit Model (Binary) This is a binary classifier that predicts the probability of a customer returning to purchase a new vehicle. Model 4: Toyota Return to Purchase Revenue Model (6 Class Multi-class) This is a multi-class classifier that predicts the spending potential of a customer after the customer is predicted to return for a purchase of a new vehicle. This generates the probabilities for 6 different classes. A final spending value is predicted after complex data processing considering probabilities for all classes and their average purchase value. Some of the most important data sources for building these models are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data.

name: Toyota In-Market Models
listdetail: The Toyota In-Market Models predict how likely a customer is to purchase a Toyota vehicle by a specific series or segment type within the next 12 months. This applies to current Toyota owners and those who previously owned a Toyota in the last 15 years, but no longer own one today. These models help Marketing teams plan and execute in-market campaigns to existing customers and their lookalikes. It also helps optimize media-spend by enabling targeted marketing. For customers predicted to be in-market, each model will return the probability that the customer will purchase a particular series or vehicle segment. Using this probability, we can determine how strong a customer''s in-market signal is. Depending on the business use case, the customer''s signal strength enables strategies that target only the most in-market customers. All the models consist of Machine Learning (ML) data based on patterns & trends. Some of the most significant data sources for building these models are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, and New Car Sales VIN Based Actuals Data.

name: Customer Segmentation Models
listdetail: Customer Segmentation is a set of models that group customers into relevant segments depending on their association with the Toyota and Lexus brand. It is designed to understand customers at a segment level, optimize business processes and operations, and improve marketing campaign effectiveness. Segmentation models consider multiple attributes based on customer purchase and service history with Toyota. Each customer is assigned to exactly one segment and sub-segment. Each segment of customers is homogeneous within and heterogeneous between other segments. When a customer is in the "Own" stage of the Shop-Buy-Own process, they would have higher-dimensional data available, which could be segmented in various ways. Understanding our customers better will enable us to improve our processes and spend according to their needs. This model contains both Toyota and Lexus data. Some of the most important data sources for building these models are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, and Customer Call Center.

name: Customer Migration Model
listdetail: The Migration Model predicts the top 4 vehicle series and trims for Toyota and/or Lexus that existing customers will most likely purchase in the next 6 months. Based on a customer''s purchase history, service/RO history, demographics, communication history, and lead/handraiser history, this model formulates the probability that the customer will purchase a vehicle different than his/her current vehicle (e.g. Toyota Camry XLE to Toyota Tundra TRD or brand change to Lexus). It does not contain migration data from Toyota/Lexus models to non-TMNA models (e.g. Honda, Nissan, etc). The purpose of this model is to help marketing teams choose the most impactful vehicle images (even the most appropriate trim) in the first touch Toyota Relationship management (RM) repurchase email program. Output from this model is also used in cross-brand tiering. Some of the most important data sources for building these models are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, and Customer Call Center.

name: Customer Defection Model
listdetail: The Defection Model is used to evaluate how long a household has owned a vehicle and use that information to predict the likelihood of the household disposing of that vehicle within the next 6 months. A household has defected from Toyota when it has disposed of all its Toyota/Scion vehicles. The purpose of this model is to reach out to households prior to leaving the Toyota/Lexus brand. This model leverages 'time-to-event' modeling procedures. The model gives each household a 90-day waiting period before it considers the household to be a defector. Data used by this model include: - VIN-Customer association - Household Demographics - Household's Prior purchase history, including - Number of previously owned Lexus Vehicles - Number of previously owned Toyota Vehicles - Ownership length - Handraiser events since last purchase Some of the most-important data sources for building this model are Customer Demographics Data and Customer-Dealer Relationship Data .

name: Lexus Customer Loyalty Models
listdetail: The Lexus Customer Loyalty Models predict the probability of a customer returning for a service or purchase of a new Lexus vehicle. This is relevant for all customers who currently own or have owned a Lexus in the past. Customers who repair or buy parts from a Lexus Dealer have a higher likelihood of buying another Lexus vehicle. In this feature, there are two different stages: Owner Segmentation and Predictive Modeling. Owner Segmentation: Lexus owners are segmented based on their current relationship and recent activities with Lexus Dealerships. Predictive Modeling: Predicts the likelihood that a Lexus customer will return for purchase or service, as well as future growth potential at a customer level. \n\nSome of the most important data sources for building this model are Customer Demographics Data, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, and Customer Call Center.

name: Customer Descriptive Score
listdetail: With the Customer Descriptive Score Model, we can gain a comprehensive view of customer profile data regarding ownership, service, and engagement, which is essential for all aspects of customer interaction with the Toyota and Lexus brands. This model is based on a customer's transactional behavior, which is broken down into the following scores. Customer Ownership Score: A score indicating a customer's association with Toyota ownership. The calculation is based on factors such as historical ownerships, purchases, memberships, and associations. Service RFM Score: This is a score reflecting the customer's historical interactions with service repair. It is calculated based on various factors such as Recency, Frequency, and Monetary aspects of the service visits. Engagement Score: A score based on the customer's activity and usage of our products and services. Survey Score: This score reflects a customer's level of satisfaction with a product, service, or support interaction based on survey responses. Some of the major sources for this data model are Customer Demographics Data, Toyota Service History USA, Lexus Service History USA, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, and Customer Call Center.

name: eBoM Reporting
listdetail: The Gold Standard Bill of Materials (BoM) Dashboard is comprised of reports that help in decision making through analysis of BoM structure and product (vehicle and non-vehicle) cost information. Reports are available on demand (on-line) and on a regular schedule. The on-online reports provide the DataMart refresh details and schedule report details - for the last run and for the next run. Also available are cumulative part usage and cost based on VIN and non-vehicle production data using the production date range supplied by the user and various reports summarizing differences between the eBoM system calculations and the General Ledger (GL) balances. The scheduled reports are used to compare two different costed BoM, schedule the HON report, report HON LE and MFG data to be used as input source to HON Hyperion Cube, schedule the standard BoM report for all vehicle and non-vehicle data, and schedule the uncosted BoM report for vehicle data.

This aids in quickly identifying areas of opportunity and risk. The report shows Rank, Share, and Sales with period over period comparison percentages and indicators (e.g. current month-to-date (MTD) vs. prior MTD, or current MTD vs MTD for the same time last year). name: Step Zero Dynamic Diagnostics Assistant
listdetail: This dashboard provides a list of recommended Original Failed Parts (OFP) and Replacement Parts for a given Vehicle Configuration to increase Technician efficiency, speed up diagnosis and repair, and identify emerging repair trends. By reducing the number of repeat repairs based on historical warranty and diagnostics data, the recommendations can reduce warranty costs (a study found that repeat repairs are about 7% of warranty costs), improve the Dealer Service Rating, increase customer satisfaction and retention, and boost the Fix it Once, Fix it Right ratio. Based on Model, Model Year, Engine, Drive Train, Transmission and Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC), the dashboard will provide a list of recommendations that include Parts, Parts Description, Confidence Score, the Number of Successful Repair Claims, and Repeat Repairs.

name: Data Communication Module Replacement List
listdetail: This API can provide you with a list of successfully onboarded Data Communication Modules (DCMs) that have been replaced by a Toyota technician. name: Customer Survey - Sentiment and Emotion Detection Model
listdetail: The Sentiment Analysis and Emotion Detection Model provides insight into a customer's experience with a product or interaction with a company representative and identifies weak links that cause negative reactions. With its Voice of the Customer (VOC) text analytics and natural language processing (NLP) capabilities, this model significantly reduces the time and effort required to gain insights into unstructured text-based data. Sentiment Analysis scores each verbatim on the strength of positive or negative sentiment, enabling us to classify the texts as “Positive”, “Negative”, or “Neutral”. This type of feedback helps us create a positive customer experience in the future and drive continuous improvement. Emotion Detection identifies five emotions based on the words used verbatim: “Happy”, “Sad”, “Fear”, “Anger”, and “Surprise”. This enables you to prioritize feature categories based on the strength-of-feeling in addition to category prevalence across the customer base. Some of the most important data sources for building this model are US Toyota Survey Data, US Lexus Survey Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Customer Call Center, and Quality Campaigns.

name: Customer Survey - Topic Model
listdetail: This Customer Survey Topic Model can provide you with insights into trending topics and sub-topics that help deliver exactly what your customers need and increase positive business results. Utilizing Voice of the Customer (VOC) text analytics and natural language processing (NLP) capabilities, this model significantly reduces the time and effort required to gain an understanding of unstructured text-based data. Below are some high-level features of the model: The Unsupervised Topic modeling feature provides insight into the topics that are trending in a set of verbatims. Sub-topics enable you to dig deeper into each of those topics. This solution is purely data-driven – it analyzes the data itself without relying on any external information or domain knowledge. The Semi-Supervised Topic modeling feature enables you to guide the analysis of your data to capture certain expected topics. By doing so, it provides the benefits of supervised learning without requiring expensive and time-consuming data labeling. Semi-Supervised modeling corresponds to the historical Product Quality Survey (PQS) categories and subcategories, which facilitates analysis of the Feature Comments data based on these categories. The subtopics bring out themes within the topics themselves and provide insight into any verbatims that do not neatly fit into existing categories. Some of the most important data sources for building this model are US Toyota Survey Data, US Lexus Survey Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Customer Call Center, and Quality Campaigns.

name: Customer Survey - Top Keyword Extraction Model
listdetail: Using the Product Quality Survey (PQS) coding feature, you can categorize the customer PQS feature comments according to the customer PQS features they mention, such as a rear seat, moonroof, or navigation system. It captures both the high-level feature category (e.g. “Seats”) and the more specific feature (e.g. “Arm Rest”). Unsupervised topic modeling uncovers the main themes or topics existing across the dataset at various levels of detail without making prior assumptions about the output. Semi-supervised topic modeling uses domain knowledge to guide the model toward specific desired themes. Additionally, the Sentiment and Emotion Detection Model provides additional insight into the customer responses at the response, vehicle feature, or topic level. The data used for PQS Feature Coding consists of PQS Survey responses from 2003-present. Using the Keyword Extraction coding feature, you can analyze which features are trending and explore what customers are saying about them. Additionally, it can be useful for locating verbatims that mention a certain feature or contain a particular phrase. Some of the most important data sources for building this model are US Toyota Survey Data, US Lexus Survey Data, Vehicle Configuration Data, Customer-Dealer Relationship Data, Customer Call center, and Quality Campaigns.

name: Toyota Quality Communication Network Report Routing
listdetail: Using this model, we can predict when a specific product may experience technical issues, which helps us develop a solution to improve product quality. This model automates the routing of field reports to Quality Assurance departments (QA). Presently, field reports must be read and assigned manually to the appropriate QA department and/or engineer. Based on NLP (Natural Language Processing), the model learns from historical reports and routes new reports accordingly. Patterns are learned based on the TQCN Report Title, Description, Part Description, Model Name, and Model Year. A set of APIs provides the recommended QA Department, Priority, and Engineer via output that is integrated with the TQCN Application.\n\nThe most important data sources for building this model are Quality Reports .

name: Brake Vibration Model
listdetail: This Brake Vibration Model is used for assessing the correlation between vehicle operation and brake warranty occurrences. name: Smart Window ETA Model
listdetail: The Smart Window ETA model predicts when a vehicle will be delivered to the dealer at various stages of its lifecycle, starting with dealer assignment and continuing until it is delivered to the dealer. By using a predictive ETA, we can reduce wasted overhead and transportation delays, as well as make informed decisions concerning inventory planning. The delivery window is updated at major manufacturing and transportation events to provide an accurate estimated delivery window at dealerships from the time of dealer assignment through the manufacturing process and transportation journey. This algorithm is based on Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (UETA) data using events from the most recent 90 days for hundreds of vehicles. Only valid VINs were analyzed during data processing (i.e. those with a valid delivery code). Traded vehicles are taken into account only once they have been delivered for the first time. Any VINs with a "hold" have been filtered out. A tree-based modeling approach has been used to predict time-to-delivery from events received for each VIN. The clusters of points obtained at different leaf nodes of the CART decision tree were explored during this process. Using a typical tree-based model, the prediction outcome is an aggregated value of observations at the leaf node. However, our analysis showed that observations at the leaf nodes are not necessarily homogeneous and follow a gamma distribution. By aggregating all of those values, hidden trends in those distributions would be masked. Therefore, we regressed the "time-to-delivery" against deciles of distributions. At leaf node, minimum window refers to absolute minimum value, and maximum window refers to x-intersection of decile regression line at one. The model predicts each VIN's every event (limited to only post-FQA events in phase 1), where a window is provided. It is most likely that vehicles will be delivered between the Start Date and the End Date of windows.

name: Service Connect Electronic Control Unit Values List

The data can be used to create a list of vehicle attributes or investigate Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC). The listed information includes: • Last Acquisition Mileage • Last Acquisition Date • ECU Values • Network Target Address To view all DTCs not triggered by a maintenance event for a specific VIN in Data Hub (DH), refer to the Trouble Code Prioritization API. The Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events API focuses on transmitting diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) that are triggered by specific maintenance events. For the outcome of monitored ECU values based on a VIN, view the Electronic Control Unit Monitoring Results API. For comprehensive remote vehicle diagnostics, including DTCs and Freeze Frame Data (FFD), refer to the Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics API. To authorize the reprogramming or replacement of a vehicle's ECU, please refer to the Electronic Control Unit Replacement Key Validation API.

listdetail: This API helps Private Distributors (PDs) with the correct set up for Monroney images so they can efficiently generate Monroney labels for Toyota and Lexus vehicles. Federal law mandates that a Monroney label be affixed to new vehicles with accurate information, and it is a legally binding document. This API provides multiple versions of the layout, Crash Test Rating information from the New Car Assessment Program (NCAP), Fuel Economy and Miles per Gallon (mpg) from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), basic Vehicle Data and Standard Equipment language. Once the image is generated, additional dealer information can be added, including Post Production Options (PPOs), total MSRP, shipping and final Dealer Destination information. Then the label can be printed and placed on the vehicle. This API supports the following distributors: - Toyota de Puerto Rico (TdPR) Gulf States Toyota (GST) and South East Toyota (SET) should use the Private Distributor Monroney Image API . Foreign distributors are not currently included.

name: Private Distributor Monroney Image
listdetail: This API helps Private Distributors (PDs) correctly set up the most updated version of Monroney images so they can efficiently generate Monroney labels for Toyota vehicles. As a legally binding document, the Monroney label must have specific and accurate information before it can be affixed to new vehicles. name: Electronic Control Unit Monitoring Results
listdetail: This API returns the outcome, or the result, of the monitored Electronic Control Unit (ECU) values based on the vehicle VIN. Improve vehicle service satisfaction by investigating or monitoring Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC) without the vehicle being present. The Service Lane Portal (SLP) requests remote monitoring of sensors through Data Hub (DH) and returns VIN, ECU ID, ECU Name, and Monitoring Details. To view all DTCs not triggered by a maintenance event for a specific VIN in Data Hub (DH), refer to the Trouble Code Prioritization API. The Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events API focuses on transmitting diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) that are triggered by specific maintenance events. For comprehensive remote vehicle diagnostics, including DTCs and Freeze Frame Data (FFD), refer to the Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics API. To access a list of ECU values for a specific VIN, including last acquisition mileage, date, ECU values, and network target address, consult the Service Connect Electronic Control Unit Values List API. To authorize the reprogramming or replacement of a vehicle's ECU, please refer to the Electronic Control Unit Replacement Key Validation API.

name: TMMI West Paint Dashboard
listdetail: This dashboard provides an array of in-depth Toyota Motor Manufacturing, Indiana, Inc. (TMMI) West Paint reports containing information on equipment and operations essential for cost efficiency, process planning, increasing safety and productivity, improving on-time delivery, and analyzing trends. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM01 Cost Analysis by Equipment: The following report provides an overview of the costs associated with equipment. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM02 Detail Cost Analysis by Equipment Report: This report breaks down the previous list into a more detailed description of what we spent on certain equipment assets. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM03 Faults 10 to 19 Minutes Line Report: This report provides a list of all Faults that occur between 10 - 19 minutes. If a Fault lasts longer than 19 minutes, it becomes a larger issue causing extended downtime and should be escalated to a priority for repairs. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM04 Process Report: This report shows a breakdown of all the processes at the facility, along with the associated Equipment Stops and Line Stops. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM05 Major Breakdown Faults Report: This report lists the major breakdowns (anything over 19 minutes), the Build Date Start, the Line Stop, the Equipment Stop, and the Fault description. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM06 West Paint Equipment Summary Report: This report provides the number of Faults, Line Stops, and Equipment Stops across all equipment on-site. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM07 Repetitive Faults Report: This report is meant to capture repetitive equipment Faults so that we can track and resolve repair issues. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM08 Summary Floor Conveyor Report: This report contains a list of floor conveyor groups and the total amount of equipment Faults and Line Stops. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM09 Totals of All Equipment Detail Report Production: This report breaks down all equipment into major areas with the total number of Faults, Stop times, and an explanation of each Fault during production hours. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM10 Totals of All Equipment Details Report: This report breaks down all equipment into major areas with the total number of Faults, Stop times, and an explanation of each Fault that occurred throughout the entire work day. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM11 Totals of All Non-Equipment Details Report: Similar to the previous report but lists Non-Equipment downtime with the total number of Faults, Stop times, and an explanation of each Fault that occurred outside of active production. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM12 Totals Floor Conveyor Detail Report: This report contains a list of floor conveyors, along with the total amount of equipment Faults and Line Stops. TMMI Paint INT1 EOM13 Totals Robot Detail Report: It contains information about the robots on the floor, as well as Faults, Stop times, and Work Order descriptions.

(TMS) provides all levels of cost and pricing of the Model, the Factory-installed accessories, and the Post Production Options (PPOs) at the time of its initial vehicle configuration. This Reprice API service makes it possible to do simulation and updates for vehicle repositioning and vehicle windfall pricing whenever it is needed. Repositioning is a process by which business users can update the cost and pricing of the Model and factory-installed accessories of one or more vehicle series from an existing cost and price general increment (GI) phase code to another. A windfall is the result of a drop in cost and pricing of a vehicle series. To track and respond to real-time configuration and pricing updates, use the Vehicle Configuration and Pricing Change Notification API. name: Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics
listdetail: This API provides the complete vehicle diagnostics information, remotely, based on the Request ID and VIN number. It requests information from Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTC), Freeze Frame Data (FFD) and the last file from the vehicle that has not been uploaded. It returns the Request ID, outcome of the request, Requestor ID and Requestor Application. To access a list of ECU values for a specific VIN, including last acquisition mileage, date, ECU values, and network target address, consult the Service Connect Electronic Control Unit Values List API. To view all DTCs not triggered by a maintenance event for a specific VIN in Data Hub (DH), refer to the Trouble Code Prioritization API. The Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events API focuses on transmitting diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) that are triggered by specific maintenance events. For the outcome of monitored ECU values based on a VIN, view the Electronic Control Unit Monitoring Results API. For Freeze Frame Data (FFD) in relation to specific DTCs for monitoring quality and initiating recalls, please refer to the Freeze Frame Data Transmission for Vehicle Quality Monitoring API.

name: Dealer Pricing
listdetail: Dealers can find the complete dealer pricing details for a vehicle with this API service. As part of the Vehicle Inquiry Service (VIS), Dealer Pricing Info can provide users with basic invoice information about the total price of a vehicle during wholesale from Toyota Motor North America (TMNA) a franchise dealer for the submitted VIN. The information returned includes the total invoice amount and a breakdown of items included in the invoice total such as the base model price and total cost of factory-installed (FIO) or post-processing options (PPO), dealer margins, freight and fuel charges, dealer advertising costs, and any discount information. The discount information includes a discount indicator to specify the type of discount and the discount amount applied to the vehicle price. For pricing information involving vehicle sales to private distributors Southeast Toyota Distributors LLC (SET) and Gulf Sales Toyota GST), please use the Distributor Pricing API. If you need pricing and details for vehicle accessories including availability and compatibility, please view the Dealer Accessory Pricing API.

name: Enterprise Vehicle Profit Planning

listdetail: This dataset contains CMBS/CMBK (Contribution Margin by Series and Katashiki) data for Enterprise Vehicle Profit analysis that can influence executives' daily and long-term decisions. CMBS/CMBK is an Excel application that combines information from pricing calculations and other sources to produce contribution margin reports by Series and Katashiki; it tracks contribution margins and installation rates down to option and specification levels. Based on these calculations, the company can measure its ability to cover variable costs with revenue. The Index of Profitability (IDX) was developed to mask data related to profits and trends so that Toyota Financial Services (TFS) could share this information with business partners without exposing sensitive information. This data is crucial for strategic volume decisions between sales, marketing, and production to evaluate the impact on profitability.

name: Vehicle Details
listdetail: The Vehicle Details API provides comprehensive vehicle information, Retail Delivery Record (RDR) details, and Deal Finalization Portal (DFP) data through the Dealer Daily Open Access (DDOA) system. This service facilitates seamless data exchange between Toyota Motor Sales (TMS) and Dealership Management Systems (DMS), enabling dealers to access and transmit critical vehicle and sales data efficiently. In the context of vehicle incentives, the API ensures that dealers can submit and verify key components necessary for incentive eligibility. The "Deal" is a combination of the RDR, Incentive, and Toyota Financial Services (TFS) Credit Contract, when applicable. For a dealer to qualify for an incentive, all three components must match precisely. If any of these elements—the RDR, Incentive, or TFS Credit Contract—fail to align, the dealer will not be eligible for incentive payment. By leveraging the Vehicle Details API, dealerships can streamline their processes, eliminate discrepancies, and ensure that incentive payments are accurately processed for eligible dealers.

name: Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events
listdetail: This API enables remote transmission of Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) for a specific vehicle identified by its Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) when a required maintenance event is triggered. It includes key information such as service codes, system details, Engine Control Unit (ECU) identifiers, mileage, and event timestamps to ensure accurate tracking of vehicle issues. When triggered, the API sends a sequence of DTCs to the Product Quality and Service Support (PQSS) team, ensuring that the diagnostic information is logged for further quality campaign management and reporting. To view all DTCs not triggered by a maintenance event for a specific VIN in Data Hub (DH), refer to the Trouble Code Prioritization API. For the outcome of monitored ECU values based on a VIN, view the Electronic Control Unit Monitoring Results API. For comprehensive remote vehicle diagnostics, including DTCs and Freeze Frame Data (FFD), refer to the Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics API. To access a list of ECU values for a specific VIN, including last acquisition mileage, date, ECU values, and network target address, consult the Service Connect Electronic Control Unit Values List API. For Freeze Frame Data (FFD) in relation to specific DTCs for monitoring quality and initiating recalls, please refer to the Freeze Frame Data Transmission for Vehicle Quality Monitoring API. To view vehicle usage patterns and customer behavior over time, please refer to the Driving Behavior Analytics API.

name: Freeze Frame Data Transmission for Vehicle Quality Monitoring
listdetail: This API provides a snapshot of Freeze Frame Data (FFD) related to vehicle quality issues that were identified by the Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events API. It sends key diagnostic information to the PQSS (Product Quality and Service Support) team, which allows them to monitor both consistent and intermittent Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) that have been triggered by the vehicle. The Freeze Frame Data helps the PQSS team track the vehicle's performance at the time the fault occurred, ensuring that quality issues are accurately identified and addressed. This data is instrumental in initiating recalls and offers valuable insights for quality forecasting, particularly for newer vehicle models. To access complete diagnostic information across multiple data types, including DTCs, FFD, and vehicle files, refer to the Service Connect Remote Vehicle Diagnostics API. name: Chronic Hold Status
listdetail: The Chronic Hold Status API allows dealers to place a continuous hold on specific vehicles at distribution centers using the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). This is typically done during audits, model launches, or when issues with the vehicle need to be resolved before shipment. The hold prevents vehicles from processing in the National Post Production System (NPPS), delaying shipment until the issue is addressed. This API integrates with the Vehicle Model Audit (VMA) application, which dealers use to audit, record, and manage vehicle features and configurations in inventory. It is especially useful during model launches, when VMA teams may apply holds on certain vehicle models or configurations for compliance checks. Dealers use this API to manage chronic holds on vehicles, ensuring they are properly handled before shipment. After the audit is completed, if the issues are resolved, the Chronic Hold Release API removes the hold, allowing the vehicles to proceed with processing and shipment. To find a list of VINs that have been marked for audit or removed from audit in the National Post Processing System (NPPS), please refer to the Vehicle Audit Notification API.

name: Chronic Hold Release
listdetail: The Chronic Hold Release API allows dealers to release holds on specific vehicles at distribution centers using the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). Once a vehicle has been audited and any issues resolved, the API notifies the National Post Processing System (NPPS) to release the hold, resuming processing and making the vehicle available for shipment. Integrated with the Vehicle Model Audit (VMA) application, this API helps manage the lifecycle of a vehicle's journey through audits, holds, and eventual shipment, ensuring that only properly validated and compliant vehicles reach the customers. Please refer to the Chronic Hold Status API to place a temporary hold on vehicles that are either under audit or have unresolved issues (such as compliance or configuration problems). To find a list of VINs that have been marked for audit or removed from audit in the National Post Processing System (NPPS), please refer to the Vehicle Audit Notification API.

name: Supplier Pallet Build and Load Shipment Confirmation
listdetail: This API uses the Logistics Input Output System (LIOS) to exchange data between the Shipping Confirmation System (SCS) and the Warehouse Management System (WMS). This API is used by suppliers, warehouse management teams, and Toyota logistics teams to manage and confirm pallet builds and shipments in the supply chain. It has two main functions: Supplier Pallet Build and Confirmation: After the supplier builds the pallets for each order, they send the details to the Toyota shipping system via LIOS. Toyota processes the data and responds with either a confirmation ID or an error message. Supplier Load Shipment and Confirmation: After the supplier completes the load building for each trailer or route, they send the shipment information through the LIOS API. Toyota processes this and sends a confirmation ID or error response. This sequence outlines where each API fits within the end-to-end logistics operations. 1. Supplier Skid and Box Details : Provides detailed planned shipment data (skid/pallet and box level) from Toyota to suppliers and internal systems and sets the foundation by communicating what needs to be shipped, where, and how. 2. Supplier Pallet Build and Load Shipment Confirmation: Suppliers use this API to confirm pallet building and shipment loading based on the planned data received. 3. Logistics Driver Validation and Route Tracking : Validates drivers authorized to perform pickups using invitation codes and provides route details and enables real-time tracking of driver pickup activities, ensuring shipments are collected as planned. 4. Driver Route and Shipment Status : Provides Toyota plants with real-time updates on driver location, order status changes, schedule alerts, and event notifications during shipment transit. This API delivers critical metrics such as mileage, transit time, and efficiency gaps, enabling plants to monitor shipment progress and respond promptly to any disruptions. 5. Logistic Partners Abnormal Events Monitoring : Monitors for any abnormal events or disruptions during shipment transit (e.g., delays, shortages).

name: Customs Status Update for Import Declarations
listdetail: This API connects with the Automated Broker Interface (ABI) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) to deliver real-time updates on import declaration statuses. It ensures Toyota’s purchasing teams are always informed about the status of their shipments, helping to avoid delays and issues with customs clearance. By integrating seamlessly with Enterprise Resourse Planning (ERP) systems like SAP, the API automatically updates purchase orders (POs) with the latest customs information, including container IDs, declared values, and product descriptions. This streamlines the process, reduces manual data entry, improves accuracy, and ensures timely customs clearance. The Importer Security Filing Status Update API focuses on managing the Importer Security Filing (ISF) process and ensuring regulatory compliance for the entry of goods.

name: TIPS - Response
listdetail: This API enables Toyota Motor North America (TMNA) and its affiliates to respond to California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) requests efficiently and securely. It sends Data Subject Access Request (DSAR) responses toTIPS, which tracks and manages these consumer privacy requests. Integrated with OneTrust for privacy management and Experian for identity verification, the API supports key CCPA rights such as the Right to Know, Right to Opt-out, and Right to Delete personal data. The API ensures TMNA’s Data Systems, Compliance, Privacy, Legal, and TIPS Teams can process these requests in compliance with privacy laws, protecting consumer rights and Toyota’s reputation. TIPS Privacy Workflow: API Interaction Sequence: 1. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Global Privacy Control API (Privacy Signal) 2. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Request API (Log Request in System) 3. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Third Party Notifications API (Notify External Vendors) 4. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) DSAR Retrieval by ID API (Validate / Fetch DSAR Info) 5. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Opt-Out Search API (Lookup Existing Opt-Outs) 6. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Response API (Deliver Final DSAR Results)

name: Logistics Driver Validation and Route Tracking
listdetail: The Logistics Driver Validation and Route Tracking API is used by the Toyota Shipping Confirmation System (TSCS) and logistics providers or drivers to confirm supplier pickups. This API validates driver information using invitation codes and provides route confirmation at the pickup stage for logistics operations. It enables drivers to confirm and track pickup activities, ensuring that all shipments are properly documented and processed. Driver Invitation Code: A preapproved code stored in the LIOS database that is shared with Logistics Provider Systems (LPS) to validate drivers, ensuring only authorized drivers are involved in the pickup process. Driver Route Details: Provides route confirmation at the pickup stage, including specific pickup and unload locations, as well as any relevant run or schedule information. This helps logistics teams track the movement and status of shipments efficiently. This sequence outlines where each API fits within the end-to-end logistics operations: 1. Supplier Skid and Box Details : Provides detailed planned shipment data (skid/pallet and box level) from Toyota to suppliers and internal systems and sets the foundation by communicating what needs to be shipped, where, and how. 2. Supplier Pallet Build and Load Shipment Confirmation : Suppliers use this API to confirm pallet building and shipment loading based on the planned data received. 3. Logistics Driver Validation and Route Tracking: Validates drivers authorized to perform pickups using invitation codes and provides route details and enables real-time tracking of driver pickup activities, ensuring shipments are collected as planned. 4. Driver Route and Shipment Status : Provides Toyota plants with real-time updates on driver location, order status changes, schedule alerts, and event notifications during shipment transit. This API delivers critical metrics such as mileage, transit time, and efficiency gaps, enabling plants to monitor shipment progress and respond promptly to any disruptions. 5. Abnormal Logistics Events Monitoring : Monitors for any abnormal events or disruptions during shipment transit (e.g., delays, shortages).

name: Importer Security Filing Status Update
listdetail: This API receives responses from Descartes JSJ regarding Importer Security Filings (ISF) and updates the filing statuses in the U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) system, ensuring businesses stay informed about their filings and any required actions. It facilitates communication between Descartes JSJ (a customs broker) and internal systems, reconciling import entries with Automated Commercial Environment (ACE) data and other compliance programs. The API also confirms successful responses from the Customs Status Update for Import Declarations API. This API is used by organizations involved in importation, customs compliance, trade management, and logistics to monitor and manage ISF filings, ensuring compliance with U.S. customs regulations.

name: TIPS - Global Privacy Control
listdetail: The Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Global Privacy Control API is designed to capture and process real-time privacy preference signals such as the “Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information” request sent directly from a user’s browser or device. These signals are part of emerging privacy frameworks like the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) and its amendments (e.g., CPRA), as well as similar laws in Colorado, Connecticut, Texas, and Montana. When a user enables GPC in their browser or through a consent platform, this API receives the signal and logs the request into TIPS, initiating a privacy action such as opt-out of data sale or sharing. It serves as the entry point for honoring automated privacy choices and supports Toyota’s compliance with GPC requirements. TIPS Privacy Workflow: API Interaction Sequence: 1. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Global Privacy Control API (Privacy Signal) 2. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Request API (Log Request in System) 3. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Third Party Notifications API (Notify External Vendors) 4. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) DSAR Retrieval by ID API (Validate / Fetch DSAR Info) 5. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Opt-Out Search API (Lookup Existing Opt-Outs) 6. Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Response API (Deliver Final DSAR Results)

name: TIPS - Third Party Notifications
listdetail: The Toyota Integrated Privacy System (TIPS) Third Party Notifications API enables approved external entities such as vendors, partners, and service providers to notify Toyota of opt-out requests they receive directly from consumers. This ensures that privacy preferences shared with third parties are also respected within Toyota’s systems, reinforcing a consistent and unified privacy posture. When a third party processes a consumer’s opt-out or “Do Not Sell or Share My Information” request, this API is used to communicate that action to TIPS. By doing so, it helps prevent unnecessary sharing or visibility of the consumer’s personal information, providing an added layer of customer privacy protection beyond Toyota's direct interactions. name: Sales Forecast and Elasticity Model
listdetail: The Sales Forecast and Elasticity Model is a data science tool developed to help Toyota and Lexus sales teams make informed decisions about how much of a discount or financial incentive to offer customers when buying or leasing a vehicle. At its core, the model uses historical sales data and pricing trends to predict how many vehicles are likely to be sold in the future. It also measures how sensitive customers are to changes in price (known as price elasticity) at the Series, Model Year, and Region level. In addition to predicting future sales, the model also compares those predictions with actual sales results to improve its accuracy over time. It uses reliable inputs like forecast cut-off dates, past volumes, pre-incentive prices, and historical performance data to ensure the recommendations are realistic. This system allows the sales teams to explore “what-if” scenarios to prepare for different market conditions whether demand is rising, competition is offering aggressive discounts, or inventory levels are changing.

name: Customer Preferences and Permissions
listdetail: This API uses the Enterprise Customer Preference Center (ECPC) to retrieve a customer's communication preferences and permissions based on their unique customer identification number. It provides detailed information on the types of messages a customer has opted to receive such as marketing, service communications, and survey feedback categorized by communication type and subcategory. The API also specifies the customer's preferred mode of communication, including email, phone, or mail. This ensures that before a promotional message or service reminder is sent, businesses can confirm whether the customer has consented to be contacted and through which channel. By using this API, organizations can maintain compliance with customer consent preferences while delivering more personalized and respectful communications. For overall customer profile and subscription data by Customer ID, Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), and Contract ID, please refer to the Customer Communication and Subscription Preferences API.

name: Email Marketing Preferences
listdetail: This API manages email marketing preferences for Toyota and Lexus products and services in compliance with the Controlling the Assault of Non-Solicited Pornography And Marketing (CAN-SPAM) Act based on choices made by customers and prospective customers. This U.S. regulation sets the rules for sending commercial emails, grants recipients the right to opt out of future messages, and promotes responsible email marketing practices. Through this API, customer preferences such as opting in or out of marketing communications are captured and stored, enabling the customer marketing team to accurately distribute automated emails and promotions only to eligible consumers. It also ensures that customers who have unsubscribed are properly excluded from future email campaigns, helping maintain compliance and customer trust.

name: Driving Behavior Analytics
listdetail: The Driving Behavior Analytics API is used by the Connected Technologies team to transmit Direct Driving Control (DDC) and Freeze Frame Data (FFD) to the Quality 360 team. This API supports vehicle analytics for both Toyota and Lexus brands, enabling deep insights into consumer driving behavior. The data provided through this API is primarily used to generate feedback and performance insights based on personal driving history, contributing to product quality enhancement and customer satisfaction initiatives. It functions independently from diagnostic fault-triggered services, offering ongoing or event-based behavioral data rather than responding to specific vehicle faults or maintenance events. In the broader diagnostic sequence: 1. The Trouble Code Transmission for Maintenance Events API transmits Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) during maintenance events. 2. The Freeze Frame Data Transmission for Vehicle Quality Monitoring follows, sending FFD linked to those DTCs for deeper fault analysis.

name: Special Service Campaign Operation Codes
listdetail: This API provides access to service operation code information stored in the Claims Processing System (CPS) for Toyota and Lexus vehicles. It is primarily used to retrieve recall and campaign operation details for a specific Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). This data supports accurate tracking of vehicle repairs, technician labor, and campaign execution status across the service network. The API can return multiple records per VIN, as a single vehicle may be subject to more than one campaign or recall. Users can only view closed recalls after the repair has been completed. For this to occur, the claim for the repair must already be submitted, and the dealer's repair order must be fully closed. Once the dealer completes the repair via a Repair Order and submits a Warranty Claim, the relevant recall information becomes accessible, ensuring that all necessary data is available for effective tracking and management of service campaigns.

name: Employee Identity and Role Management
listdetail: This API offers a secure way to manage employee identity information tailored for internal enterprise use across Toyota's Human Resource (HR) systems and administrative tools. It allows users to easily access and manage detailed employee profiles, including personal information such as Full Name, Email Address, Employee ID, Creation Date, and associated Groups. The API tracks an employee’s timeline at Toyota, highlighting significant milestones like role changes and department transfers. It enables updates to key profile fields and retrieves application-specific employee roles, detailing each role’s name, description, and corresponding IDs for effective role-based access control. Additionally, the API facilitates onboarding by integrating new employees into defined roles within applications, ensuring efficient role management and access provisioning throughout the organization. For basic employee details like Name, Email, Creation Date, and Group Membership, please refer to the Employee Identity Lookup API. To find an employee's current job information including Job Title, Department, Manager ID, Desk Location, Building ID, Badge ID, please refer to the Workday Employee Search API.

name: Salvage Status and Warranty Eligibility
listdetail: This API is designed to identify vehicles that are no longer eligible for warranty coverage due to their salvage status. A salvage Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) indicates a vehicle that has been declared a total loss, typically because repair costs exceed its value. This API plays a critical role in helping Toyota eliminate unnecessary warranty payments by shutting off coverage on ineligible vehicles. Warranty Operations use it to block invalid claims, while Service and Field teams confirm coverage before repairs. Dealers can use this service to validate warranty eligibility, helping streamline dealership operations and reduce claim rejections. By integrating this API into their systems and workflows, these teams can enhance operational efficiency, reduce cost leakage, and uphold the integrity of Toyota’s warranty programs.

name: Customer Communication and Subscription Preferences
listdetail: This API retrieves customer communication preferences and profile details by using key identifiers such as Customer ID, Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), and Contract ID. A Contract ID is a unique identifier assigned to a specific contract held by a customer, particularly in the context of services or subscriptions. The API returns essential customer information including email and postal address, allowing systems to maintain accurate and up-to-date contact details. It also provides subscription data, indicating the specific product a customer is subscribed to, such as Remote Connect, along with its current status, effective start date, and expiration date. These dates can vary widely depending on the subscription. Additionally, the API delivers the customer’s preferred dealership and their chosen communication channels, enabling personalized and consistent engagement across Toyota’s services. To determine the customer’s preferences regarding communication with their primary dealer, preferred dealer, and home dealer, please refer to the Retrieve Customer Communication Permissions API. To retrieve more granular communication preferences, focusing specifically on a customer’s consent for different types of messages (e.g., marketing, service reminders, surveys), please refer to the Customer Preferences and Permissions API.

name: Shipment Equipment Status and Location Update
listdetail: This API communicates real-time updates to the Warehouse Management System (WMS) when there is a change to a trailer or container’s status or parking location. It provides outbound shipment data including container number, equipment ID, seal number, Standard Carrier Alpha Code (SCAC), shipment ID, loaded quantity, total weight, and hazmat indicator. Each message includes a timestamp and key identifiers for the sender, receiver, and organization such as the North American Parts Center (NAPC). This API supports outbound logistics operations by ensuring accurate and timely equipment and shipment status reporting during the packing and loading process. To monitor trailer flow within the yard and dock area, including when and where a trailer arrives, is docked, or leaves, please refer to the Trailer Status API.

By providing the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) and the product type (e.g., “Telematics Description”), the API returns the current status of that subscription, including a status type, a status code, and the timestamp of the status check. This API is ideal for systems or applications that need to quickly confirm whether a vehicle has an active subscription to a particular service. It supports functionality such as enabling or disabling connected features, validating service eligibility, and streamlining support diagnostics.

name: Repair and Maintenance Records
listdetail: This API provides a comprehensive service history for Toyota and Lexus vehicles using the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). This API is primarily used within the Claims Processing System (CPS) to evaluate vehicle care and maintenance records. It enables quality teams such as Product Quality & Service Support (PQSS) to monitor how vehicles are maintained over time, which supports quality reporting, insights for future vehicle builds, and proactive service recommendations. CPS also uses this data to determine warranty service eligibility by assessing whether a vehicle has been properly maintained according to recommended schedules. The service history includes details such as the type of service performed, effective and expiration dates, mileage limits, oil type, and current warranty status. To check past repair orders for warranty claim validation and approval, please refer to the Warranty Eligibility and Service History API.

name: Vehicle Event Submission
listdetail: This API enables Manufacturers and Private Distributors to submit real-time vehicle event updates to Toyota Enterprise Systems. This data is used by Toyota to enhance visibility into the vehicle delivery process and accurately calculate Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) at the final destination. By sending key logistics and tracking events (e.g., arrival at a transit location, shipment tendered, etc.), this API ensures Toyota systems remain synchronized with vehicle movements, improving visibility for internal teams, dealers, and customers across the supply chain. To retrieve (pull) logistics data for a vehicle using its VIN, please refer to the Vehicle Events API.

name: Customer Non-Vehicle Subscriptions
listdetail: This API delivers detailed subscription data for non-vehicle products by leveraging a combination of the Customer ID and Vehicle Identification Number (VIN). It returns essential customer service information, including the type of service plan, servicing dealer, service dates, and mileage details when available. In addition, the API provides specific non-vehicle product attributes such as product key, current status, effective and expiration dates. These services may originate from Toyota/Lexus or be sourced from third-party providers. For example, the API can return records like a SIRIUS XM subscription tied to a customer and VIN, showing service details with associated dealer, duration, and other contextual data even when certain fields, such as expiration mileage, are not applicable.

name: Parts Order Management
listdetail: This API is an integral component of the Advanced Parts System (APS), designed to assist authorized dealers in efficiently managing their parts orders submitted through the Dealer Daily platform. This API provides dealers with the ability to view the current status and details of their submitted parts orders, modify order specifics such as quantities, items, or shipping preferences, and upgrade orders for expedited processing or alternative fulfillment options. Additionally, it allows for the cancellation of parts orders in cases of changes or errors prior to fulfillment. Typical use cases for this API include scenarios where a dealer checks the fulfillment status of a pending order, updates an order to accommodate new vehicle service needs, requests an expedited shipping upgrade for a high-priority part, or cancels a mistakenly submitted order before processing. By integrating with APS, this API ensures real-time access to order information and transactional flexibility, helping streamline parts inventory management and improve order accuracy. The Certified Vehicle Parts Order API allows dealers to submit and validate parts orders for certified Toyota and Lexus vehicles.

name: Accessory Weight Compliance and Labeling
listdetail: This API service provides the total combined weight of all post-production options (PPOs) installed on vehicles after manufacturing. In compliance with regulatory requirements, Toyota Motor North America (TMNA) must inform customers of the accessory weight included in the vehicle's total weight to prevent overloading and maintain safe vehicle operation. This API enables TLS (Toyota Logistics Services) to retrieve weight data for each individual Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) and generate printed labels/stickers displaying the relevant accessory weight information. It supports labeling accuracy and compliance across the Service Parts and Accessories Development (SPAD) process.

name: Warranty Plan Validation
listdetail: This API determines the applicable warranty plan for vehicles that are eligible for certification by evaluating factors such as TRAC (Toyota Rent-A-Car) or LCCS (Lexus Customer Convenience System) status, model year, and current mileage. The API supports warranty validation for service departments, allowing them to confirm eligibility before repairs, as well as aiding in rental vehicle operations. TRAC assists dealers in offering rental vehicles to customers for service, insurance replacement, or general rental needs. LCCS enables Lexus dealers to provide service loaner vehicles and also serves as the administrative framework for placing these vehicles into loaner service. By submitting a Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), the API returns detailed warranty information, including warranty codes, descriptions, eligibility flags, coverage mileage limits, and associated plan amounts.

name: Workday Employee Search
listdetail: This API provides real-time access to accurate employee job data for internal use by team members and corporate partners. It is commonly integrated into systems such as HR platforms, IT service portals, onboarding tools, and badge access systems. When an employee’s email is submitted through this API, Workday verifies the input and returns relevant job data if a match exists; otherwise, it returns an error or no data. A standard response includes details such as Employee ID, Full Name, Badge ID, Work Email, Phone Number, Job Title, Manager ID, Department, Desk Location, Building ID, and Mail Drop. By centralizing access to this data through Workday, the API improves accuracy, reduces duplication, and enables efficient workflows across enterprise systems that depend on employee information. For comprehensive identity lifecycle management, including retrieving, updating, and onboarding user profiles, please refer to the Employee Identity and Role Management API. For basic employee details like Name, Email, Creation Date, and Group Membership, please refer to the Employee Identity Lookup API.

name: Warehouse Workload Planning
listdetail: This API is designed to streamline workload planning for Toyota Parts Center (TPC) warehouses by enabling the creation, updating, and review of warehouse workload plans. This API eliminates the need for manual planning by automating workload configuration based on warehouse efficiency metrics and manpower distribution. Users can define and manage operational parameters such as unloading and picking efficiency, units of measurement, manpower allocation, and target buffer levels across different warehouse areas and work zones. Each request identifies a target warehouse, such as Product Change Control (PCC) or Product Change Kit (PCK), and includes structured input data that encompasses warehouse areas, nested work areas, and sub-areas, as well as efficiency rates and timestamps for traceability. The API supports effective workload balancing and plan-versus-actual analysis, ensuring better resource utilization and operational visibility.

name: Dealer Allowance Program Verification
listdetail: This API enables Toyota and Lexus dealers to verify whether a sold vehicle qualifies for key sales margin programs such as the Dealer Holdback, Wholesale Financial Reserve, Delivery Allowance Program (DAP), and Covenant Allowance Program (CAP). These programs provide financial reimbursements to dealers for the time and effort spent delivering and selling a vehicle to a customer, but eligibility must be confirmed and a claim submitted before payment is issued. Integrated with the Dealer Daily (DD) system, the API supports a seamless verification process. Dealers submit a Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) through Dealer Daily and the API returns a total record count along with detailed program data such as program type, verification status (e.g., Pending, Verified), sales month, vehicle model, and series. When needed, users can also prompt the system to return vehicle configuration details, supporting accurate and complete claim submissions. Once a vehicle’s eligibility is verified, the system triggers the reimbursement workflow, and payments are typically issued within a few business days. The Dealer Allowance Program Payment Inquiry API retrieves the authorized payment details for vehicles that have been verified and approved. It shows the amount paid, payment method, date, The and transaction info, helping dealers reconcile received payments with verified vehicles.

name: Update Customer Preferences and Permissions
listdetail: This API is a service that allows external systems to update a customer’s communication preferences and permissions in the Enterprise Customer Preference Center (ECPC) system using the Customer ID. It enables setting or removing opt-outs at the brand, category, or subcategory level, and specifying preferred communication channels like email, phone, or mail. This API is typically used when a customer updates their preferences through a portal, ensuring those changes are saved and reflected in backend systems. To find the customer’s communication preferences by Customer ID, please refer to the Customer Preferences and Permissions API. To find out the customer’s communication preferences by Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), please refer to the Retrieve Customer Communication Permissions API. To save the customer’s preferred communication channel information by Customer ID, please refer to the Save Customer Communication Permissions API. For overall customer profile and subscription data by Customer ID, Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), and Contract ID, please refer to the Customer Communication and Subscription Preferences API.

name: Parts Recovery Claim Submission
listdetail: This API enables Toyota and Lexus dealers to submit claims to the Parts Recovery System (PRS). Dealers provide vehicle and dealer information, along with repair details and associated costs. Upon submission, a claim number is generated to track the approval process. After the distributor reviews and accepts the claim, the dealer may proceed with a valid parts return, depending on part eligibility such as hazmat restrictions, and may receive a transaction response (e.g. Claim Number, Claim Code, Status) from the Claims Processing System (CPS). By using this API, dealers can quickly and accurately submit required claim data without relying on manual forms or separate systems.

name: Retrieve Operational Dealership Reports
listdetail: This API is a service that retrieves various dealership-related reports from Toyota's Legacy systems. Used by dealer portals, internal systems, and back-office applications, the API serves as a bridge between modern platforms and mainframe-generated reports including data on parts, warranty, finance, vehicle management, and more. Applications such as the Dealer Portal send a Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) request to the API with key parameters such as Dealer Number, Report Type, and Transaction Date. The API then queries the Seasonally Adjusted Annual Rate (SAAR) host system and returns either the report data or a URL to the HTML-formatted report for display or download. Despite its Legacy status, the API remains in use because the underlying data still resides in Information Management System (IMS), hence the reports are standardized and pre-validated across the dealer network.

name: Electronic Control Unit Replacement Key Validation
listdetail: This API facilitates secure communication between Toyota systems during the reprogramming or replacement of a vehicle’s Electronic Control Unit (ECU). When a technician connects a Global Techstream (GTS) device to a vehicle, it sends safety key identifiers to Product Quality & Service Support (PQSS). PQSS then uses this API to request the corresponding Manual Allocation Code (MAC) key information from Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC). After TMC’s quality team authenticates the request, the necessary key data is returned, allowing authorization of a new or replacement ECU. This API ensures that the key exchange process is handled securely and efficiently, supporting accurate and authorized ECU updates. To access a list of ECU values for a specific VIN, including last acquisition mileage, date, ECU values, and network target address, consult the Service Connect Electronic Control Unit Values List API. For the outcome of monitored ECU values based on a VIN, view the Electronic Control Unit Monitoring Results API.

listdetail: This API retrieves and compares invoices posted in Ariba with those recorded in SAP to support automated reconciliation. Together, they facilitate reliable synchronization between legacy systems and current platforms, supporting financial continuity across the organization.

name: Goods and Parts Quantity Synchronization
listdetail: This API transfers Goods Parts Quantity (GPQ) data from the Manufacturing Operations Management (MOM) system to the SAP inventory module. It enables seamless integration between production operations and enterprise resource planning, helping vehicle plants maintain accurate inventory and optimize material planning. The payload includes key production details such as material codes, production dates, plant codes, and work order IDs, which SAP uses for inventory updates, production confirmations, and order management. This sequence outlines where each API fits within the end-to-end manufacturing process. 1. Manufacturing Sales Order Submission : SAP sends confirmed sales orders to MOM to trigger production planning. 2. Manufacturing Sales Order Acknowledgements : MOM confirms receipt and processing of the sales order to SAP. 3. Goods and Parts Quantity Synchronization: MOM manufactures goods, sends GPQ data - MOM reports the actual quantities of parts produced to SAP for inventory and production tracking. 3A. Manufacturing Shift Delivery Information : Provides SAP and accounting teams with a detailed breakdown of all manufacturing operations completed during a shift. 4. Material Usage Variance : MOM sends actual vs. planned material usage data to SAP for cost and inventory control. 5. Finished Goods Shipment Confirmation : SAP notifies MOM that finished goods have been shipped to customers or distribution centers.

name: Mirai Loaner Rental Status and Claims Tracking
listdetail: Using the Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), this API delivers real-time status updates and remaining rental day details for vehicles enrolled in the Mirai Loaner Program. This API enables dealers and program administrators to efficiently monitor loaner vehicle usage, availability, and claim processing, ensuring seamless management of the program. The Mirai Loaner Program offers temporary replacement vehicles exclusively from the new and unlicensed MY25 Mirai lineup, including demonstration models with 20,000 miles or less. Eligible vehicles must be purchased or leased directly from dealer ground stock inventory within the program period and registered with the California State Department of Motor Vehicles. The program runs from August 5, 2025, through September 2, 2025. All credit applications related to the program require approval by Toyota Financial Services (TFS). The Claims Processing System (CPS) integrated with this API manages and tracks claims associated with loaner vehicles, including rental days, sublet types, invoice amounts, and rental reasons. By providing a centralized platform for claim data, CPS supports accurate billing, reimbursement, and compliance with program eligibility requirements. Overall, this API streamlines the administration of the Mirai Loaner Program by combining real-time vehicle status monitoring with comprehensive claims processing, enhancing dealer efficiency and customer satisfaction while promoting Toyota’s commitment to sustainable hydrogen fuel cell technology.

name: Sales Order Batch Processing
listdetail: This API facilitates asynchronous batch handling, creation, and processing of sales orders within the SAP system for vehicles, parts, and services. By decoupling order submission from immediate processing, it optimizes system performance and enables SAP to handle high transaction volumes without sacrificing responsiveness or stability. When a sales order request is received, the API quickly returns a confirmation number. The complete order creation and processing then take place later in the background through SAP batch jobs or queues. This asynchronous design helps Finance and Accounting teams by ensuring reliable order intake while preventing system bottlenecks during peak times. Orders can include detailed information such as vehicle identification numbers (VINs), purchase order details, customer data, financial amounts, dealer charges, quantities, billing descriptions, sold-to customer accounts, and the originating system or channel. By leveraging this API, organizations can streamline sales order management, reduce manual effort, and maintain SAP system performance under heavy load ensuring timely and accurate processing of vehicle, parts, and service orders.

name: Vehicle Configuration and Accessory Changes
listdetail: This API provides updated specifications for Toyota and Lexus vehicle series that have changed since a specified date. It delivers comprehensive data including full vehicle configurations, In-Line Accessories (ILAs), and distributor details. This API is designed to help dealers and Private Distrubutors (PDs) access the latest information on vehicles and their respective accessories available in the production pipeline. By using this data, they can better fulfill customer orders and manage inventory allocation based on current market interest. The API works by accepting a date parameter to identify vehicle series whose specifications have changed since that date. Upon receiving a request, it queries the database for updated Toyota and Lexus series data and returns relevant information such as model year, distributor codes, detailed model, katashiki, and specification data, along with key dates like order basis end and lineoff end. This enables accurate tracking of the latest vehicle specs and supports effective planning, production, and order management. To track and respond to real-time configuration and pricing updates, use the Vehicle Configuration and Pricing Change Notification API. Use the Vehicle Configuration and Reprice API to simulate or apply pricing updates across VINs for business processes like repositioning or windfall pricing.

name: Battery Quality and Performance
platform: TBDP (IRM, PASA, C360, Q360, IRM-Pricing, etc.)
listdetail: This dataset contains detailed measurements and inspection data related to battery parts, primarily used for quality control, performance evaluation, and predictive analysis in battery manufacturing or testing processes. It includes a comprehensive set of electrical characteristics such as initial and final charge levels, voltage measurements at multiple stages, and internal resistance values, which are critical indicators of battery health and aging. In addition to electrical data, the dataset incorporates extensive visual and surface inspection results, including top surface checks and offline appearance inspections, to identify physical defects or anomalies. Statistical quality control metrics, such as sigma judgment and internal resistance validation, are also included to ensure data reliability and manufacturing consistency. Material tracking and status codes provide traceability of battery components and their production quality, enabling effective monitoring of pass/fail outcomes during the manufacturing process. Overall, this dataset supports advanced analysis and modeling efforts aimed at improving battery reliability, optimizing production quality, and predicting battery performance over time.

Designed for eligible Lexus vehicles, this API tracks service milestones from 5,000 to 25,000 miles and provides detailed insights including Vehicle Identification Number (VIN), mileage, service status, dealer ID, and more. It ensures reliable, consistent tracking of vehicle care, enhancing the ownership experience and supporting long-term vehicle performance. To track services performed under the ToytaCare program for all eligible purchased or leased Toyota vehicles, refer to the ToyotaCare Service Information API.

name: Automated Call-In System Employee Absence Reporting
listdetail: The Automated Call-In System (ACS) Employee Absence Reporting API provides centralized and standardized access to employee absence data, specifically designed to support North American Manufacturing Centers (NAMCs). By integrating seamlessly with absence management systems, it delivers detailed insights into call-in activity, enabling Group Leaders (GLs) and higher management to accurately assess manpower requirements before production begins. The API captures essential information including Workday ID, employee name, department, business unit, cost center, reason for absence, confirmation number, submission date, and record status, offering clear and comprehensive visibility into workforce availability across multiple facilities. The Employee Call-In and Shift Absence Management API is more operational, providing shift managers with timely absence and return dates plus contact info to manage daily team schedules effectively. For a visual, user-friendly tool to help supervisors and Human Resource (HR) staff monitor daily call-ins and track absenteeism trends, use the Automated Call-In System Dashboard .
